sentence: This project studies exotic collective phenomena in quantum systems using superconducting circuits, trapped ultracold atoms and quantum materials.
This project tries to find out what three-dimensional shapes RNA molecules take in human cells and how those shapes help control genes.
This project builds batteryless sensor prototypes that use kinetic energy harvesting and deep learning to analyze data from wearable devices.
This project tests teaching methods that use guided inquiry and collaborative design studios in computer architecture courses.
This project studies how a signaling pathway shared by flies, worms, fish and humans meets the different needs of different tissues.
This project studies how brain-inspired spiking neural networks can learn tasks that happen in sequence by treating them as event-driven dynamical systems.
This project studies how particles driven by concentration gradients move in self-organizing reaction-diffusion patterns, and how motion and patterns disrupt each other.
This project examines topics in science, technology, engineering and mathematics education, such as biotechnology visual literacy, bioinformatics assessment and computational literacy.
This project builds tools that read expanded genetic alphabets and tries to find out how a microbial host copes with unnatural base pairs.
This project builds a supercomputer system for artificial intelligence and data intensive research, including drug discovery, digital agriculture and turbulence in fusion.
This project builds a method that tests many predictive algorithms, keeps those that predict well enough, and measures how stable the conclusions from data are.
This project builds machine learning methods that find cause-and-effect relationships in complex data, even when some data are missing or hidden variables are present.
This project builds a system that uses robotic arms for 3D printing to control the direction of composite materials inside a part.
This project looks for evidence of settlement and maize farming at a site, using remote sensing, ground penetrating radar, excavations and soil samples.
This project builds a mean-field model and computer simulations that predict the structure of materials made by assembling nanoparticles.
